title: Parallel motion as an exact counterfactual
question: How much of the cross-view geometry do feed-forward models use for a moving object?
caption: (a) **The counterfactual.** A point moving parallel to the camera baseline by s b and a static point at X/(1-s) project to the same pixels in both views. (b) **A parallel mover.** A mover in CONVOY-3D and the depth a model predicts for it from both views. (c) **Prior or geometry.** Log depth error against the geometric answer x = -log(1-s), binned medians over purely parallel movers: a model that used only geometry would follow the diagonal, a model that uses only its single-image prior stays at zero.
caption_plain: (a) The counterfactual. A point moving parallel to the camera baseline by s b and a static point at X/(1-s) project to the same pixels in both views. (b) A parallel mover. A mover in CONVOY-3D and the depth a model predicts for it from both views. (c) Prior or geometry. Log depth error against the geometric answer x = -log(1-s), binned medians over purely parallel movers: a model that used only geometry would follow the diagonal, a model that uses only its single-image prior stays at zero.
caption_tex: \textbf{Parallel motion as an exact counterfactual.} (a) \textbf{The counterfactual.} A point moving parallel to the camera baseline by $s\,\mathbf{b}$ and a static point at $X/(1-s)$ project to the same pixels in both views. (b) \textbf{A parallel mover.} A mover in CONVOY-3D and the depth a model predicts for it from both views. (c) \textbf{Prior or geometry.} Log depth error against the geometric answer $x=-\log(1-s)$, binned medians over purely parallel movers: a model that used only geometry would follow the diagonal, a model that uses only its single-image prior stays at zero.

title: Testbeds and the checks that make the probe interpretable
question: Do the models reconstruct the static scene of each testbed, and does the estimator recover a known answer?
caption: (a)-(c) **Testbeds.** CONVOY-3D (ray-cast streets), CONVOY-REAL (real TUM images and their measured depth, with inserted movers of exact depth) and Virtual KITTI 2 (photo-realistic driving); top: first view with the movers outlined by their exact motion regime, bottom: ground-truth depth. (d) **Validity gate.** Medians over images of AbsRel and of the log-depth slope on static pixels; the shaded box is the pre-registered pass region, and LEGACY-FLAT falls outside it for every model. (e) **Estimator check.** Predictors with a planted prior weight w recover the slope-weight identity (largest deviation 0.000), so beta_s reads as a geometry share.

(d) Validity gate. Medians over images of AbsRel and of the log-depth slope on static pixels; the shaded box is the pre-registered pass region, and LEGACY-FLAT falls outside it for every model. (e) Estimator check. Predictors with a planted prior weight w recover the slope-weight identity (largest deviation 0.000), so beta_s reads as a geometry share.

title: How much geometry the models use

caption: (a) **Geometry share.** beta_s of every model for purely parallel movers in CONVOY-3D (95% cluster-bootstrap intervals), the same model's single-image prediction (open circles) and classical triangulation with the true pose from exact correspondences and from RAFT-large optical flow (triang., flow); the top axis gives the equivalent prior weight, the shaded band is the range the locked Prediction 1 expected. title: Qualitative: what geometry and the prior see
question: Why do geometric masks miss parallel movers, and what does the single-image prediction add?
caption: (a) **Parallel mover.** A CONVOY-3D mover with ε = 0: it leaves no geometric residual, so M2 cannot flag it. (b) **Perpendicular mover.** A mover off its epipolar line: M2 flags it whatever depth the model predicts. (c) **Driving.** A moving Virtual KITTI 2 vehicle (exact depth and poses). **Layout.** Crops around a mover (DUSt3R); depth panels share one colour scale per row. **Reading the masks.** M2 and M5 are divided by their 5% false-positive threshold on the static pixels of the same image, so values above 1 are detections. **What it shows.** A parallel mover leaves no geometric residual; the disagreement between the two-view and the single-image depth (M5) can still mark it when the model follows geometry.

title: The static twin and the ground plane
question: Where is the static twin of a grounded mover, and how much invisible motion does it expose?
caption: (a) **The static twin.** Side view of Proposition 4: a grounded object moving with the camera (s = 0.5) is explained by a static twin that is twice as large and whose contact lies H s/(1-s) below the road (H: camera height above the object's contact plane); the road would hide it. An oncoming object (s < 0) has a twin floating above the road. (b) **Twin height.** Height of the twin's contact over H, against s: the law -s/(1-s) and Argoverse 2 vehicles in the parallel regime (camera height from each vehicle's labelled box, x_geo from its LiDAR pixels and labelled motion); shaded: the 95% range of parked vehicles. (c) **Twin test by s.** Share of moving Argoverse 2 vehicles flagged by the epipolar test (|eps| above its 95th percentile over parked vehicles, 0.54 px), by the twin test (|twin height| above its 95th percentile, 0.30 m) and by either, binned by s; dotted: the twin test's detection curve for exactly parallel motion implied by the parked vehicles. (d) **Labels vs flow.** Parallel-regime vehicles flagged by each test (bars: epipolar, twin, either; 95% intervals over vehicle tracks) with the exact correspondences of panels (b-c) and with optical flow (RAFT-large, forward-backward checked) and the road plane fitted to the LiDAR returns instead of the labelled box; both at 5% false positives on parked vehicles. H14: twin minus epipolar with flow +0.21 [+0.13, +0.29] over 543 vehicles, SUPPORTED.

title: Two channels: contact and parallax
question: Does one cue-combination model with a contact channel and a parallax channel explain every testbed?
caption: (a) **Out of sample.** The cue model rho - rho_mono = w (x - rho_mono), w = c_support d^2/(d^2 + kappa^2), fitted on CONVOY-3D and the E5 conditions, predicts the slope of every other testbed from that testbed's own objects (geometric answer, single-image error, parallax, support) without refitting; observed slope (95% interval) against predicted slope (Pearson r = 0.91, mean absolute error 0.05; open markers: the new designed sets). (b) **The hump.** Median rho of CONVOY-3D parallel movers by x (markers) and the fits of the two-channel model (solid) and of the contact-only model with constant weight (dashed), for DUSt3R and MASt3R; in the two-channel model, any fall at large x comes from the parallax, which vanishes as s approaches 1; fall from the observed peak to the largest x: DUSt3R 0.18 observed, -0.03 two channels, -0.09 contact only, MASt3R 0.21 observed, -0.11 two channels, -0.13 contact only. (c) **Two channels.** Fitted share of geometry at unlimited parallax for objects with the contact in view (open circles), with the contact hidden (triangles) and floating, i.e. without support (squares), and the half-saturation parallax kappa in px (right). (d) **Masks.** Change of M2 recall against the change of beta_s between conditions of the same movers (E5 conditions against grounded, baseline levels against x0.5, wall heights against no wall); Spearman -0.71. Exploratory (AMENDMENT_V6_5).

title: Designed experiments: parallax and contact, one at a time
question: Does a longer baseline alone raise the geometry share, and does the lowest wall that hides the contact suffice?
caption: (a) **One factor at a time.** Top: the second view of one baseline-sweep scene at 0.5 and 3 times the baseline (first view, s, eps = 0 and the geometric answer are identical); bottom: one mover behind the 15 cm and the 70 cm wall. title: Real objects that float
